headline: Public docs teardown: highest-impact fixes and the automation layer to prioritize first

summary.executive_summary: Audit of docs.readme.com crawled 365 pages (100% coverage). 3 broken internal links confirmed; 124 links remain unverified due to auth/rate-limit blocks. API reference coverage is critically low at 4.65% despite 153 API pages detected. Only 32.6% of pages display last-updated metadata, creating stale-risk exposure of 66.78%. Retrieval readiness scores 72.23 (moderate band), with chunkability at 63.84% limiting AI answer quality.

key_findings.headline: Undocumented API operations
key_findings.business_consequence: Generate/update reference + how-to from OpenAPI and enforce drift checks.

key_findings.headline: Documentation freshness debt
key_findings.business_consequence: Prioritize stale pages via weekly SLA loop and lifecycle policies.

key_findings.headline: Code/docs contract drift
key_findings.business_consequence: Track interface changes and enforce docs updates with report-first governance.

priority_actions.title: Inject last-updated timestamps into the 67.4% of pages missing freshness metadata to reduce stale-risk from 66.78% below 20%
priority_actions.why_this_first: Low-effort metadata addition immediately boosts user trust, reduces support queries about outdated content, and improves retrieval readiness score by 10+ points.

priority_actions.title: Add usage examples, parameters, and integration guides to the 153 detected API pages to lift reference coverage from 4.65% toward 60%+
priority_actions.why_this_first: Closing the 95% API documentation gap directly unblocks developer onboarding, reduces support tickets, and improves time-to-first-call for new users.

priority_actions.title: Fix the 3 confirmed broken internal links and establish auth-bypass crawling to verify the 124 unverified URLs
priority_actions.why_this_first: Repairing navigation and uncovering hidden broken links prevents user drop-off and lifts link confidence from 25% to 80%+, improving SEO and user flow.

strengths: Complete crawl coverage (365/365 pages, 100%) with no significant trap patterns
Example code reliability estimate at 100% with no detection issues flagged
Strong answerability (100%) and citationability (100%) for AI retrieval
risks: API reference coverage at 4.65% leaves 95% of 153 API pages without usage documentation, blocking developer onboarding
66.78% stale-risk exposure due to missing last-updated dates on 67.4% of pages, eroding user trust
124 unverified links (auth/rate-limit blocked) may hide additional broken links beyond the 3 confirmed
Chunkability at 63.84% limits RAG/AI answer quality and search relevance for 36% of content
limitations: External audit cannot verify the 124 auth-gated or rate-limited links; actual broken link count may be higher than the 3 confirmed.
API coverage detection relies on heuristics; the 4.65% figure assumes correct identification of all 153 API pages and may undercount edge cases.
Freshness and stale-risk metrics depend on visible last-updated metadata; actual content age may differ if updates occur without timestamp changes.
automation_first: Deploy CI/CD link checker with auth-bypass for the 124 unverified URLs and continuous monitoring of the 3 confirmed broken links, preventing future navigation failures and lifting link confidence from 25% to 90%+ with zero manual effort per release.

Automate last-updated timestamp injection via Git commit metadata for the 246 pages (67.4%) missing freshness data, eliminating the 66.78% stale-risk exposure and ensuring every page shows accurate recency without writer intervention.

Implement automated API reference linting to flag the 146 API pages (95.4% of 153) lacking usage examples, parameters, or code samples, creating a pre-publish gate that prevents API coverage from regressing below 60% and reduces developer onboarding friction.
